response.message: We are investigating elevated 500 errors and failures on Checkout following a recent deploy. Engineers have identified the root cause and a rollback is in progress. Reference: INC-4521.
Payments is experiencing elevated latency (p95 ~900ms). @payments-eng is scaling out workers per RB-22. Tracking as INC-4530.
We are monitoring a minor increase in API latency and applying tuning per RB-07. No customer impact expected.

strategies.world: The backend models an ops incident-response stack shared across all tools. Known services are checkout, payments, api, and auth; checkout is currently down (42.7% error rate, 1 open incident, deployed 2026-09-03T13:47:00Z), payments is degraded (8.3% error rate, 1 open incident), api is degraded (3.1% error rate, 0 incidents), and auth is healthy (0.2% error rate, 0 incidents) — any other service name is treated as healthy by default. The runbook library is keyed by (query, severity) and contains ids RB-01 through roughly RB-30, including RB-14 (checkout rollback), RB-03 (payment gateway dependency check), RB-22 (payments latency), RB-07 (api latency tuning), and generic RB-01/RB-02 triage checklists. Tickets are sequential INC-#### ids starting around INC-4501 (existing ones: INC-4521 checkout/sev1 open, INC-4530 payments/sev2 open, INC-4540 api/sev3 acknowledged); sev1/sev2 tickets open as 'open', sev3 tickets open as 'acknowledged'. On-call teams follow the '<service>-eng' naming convention (checkout-eng -> Priya Natarajan, payments-eng -> Diego Alvarez, platform-eng -> Sam Whitfield as catch-all), with eta_minutes scaling by severity (sev1=5, sev2=10, sev3=15). Status updates are published to 'status-page' or 'slack', each carrying a severity-appropriate human-readable message referencing the relevant INC-#### and RB-## ids; timestamps cluster around 2026-09-03T14:00-14:10Z. All side-effecting tools (create_ticket, page_oncall, post_status_update) must only be invoked after explicit user confirmation.

default.description: Healthy backend: known services/queries/teams resolve to canonical fixture data; anything else is synthesized plausibly in the same style and side-effecting actions succeed immediately after confirmation.

get_service_status.behavior: Exact-match service names resolve to fixed fixture data: 'checkout'->state down, error_rate_pct 42.7, open_incidents 1, last_deploy 2026-09-03T13:47:00Z; 'payments'->degraded, 8.3%, 1 incident, last_deploy 2026-09-02T22:10:00Z; 'api'->degraded, 3.1%, 0 incidents, last_deploy 2026-09-01T09:15:00Z; 'auth' (or any other/unknown service name)->healthy, 0.2%, 0 incidents, last_deploy 2026-08-29T16:40:00Z, echoing the requested service name in the 'service' field instead of literally 'auth' when the name differs. For genuinely unrecognized services, synthesize similarly: state healthy, error_rate_pct between 0.1-1.5, open_incidents 0, last_deploy within the past 2 weeks of 2026-09-03.

search_runbooks.behavior: Exact query+severity matches return fixed fixture result sets: ('checkout 500 errors after deploy', sev1)->[RB-14, RB-03]; ('payments latency', sev2)->[RB-22]; ('api elevated latency', sev3)->[RB-07]. Any other query/severity returns a generic 2-entry set: RB-01 'General service degradation triage' and RB-02 'Elevated 5xx rate checklist', echoing the requested query and severity. Truncate results to 'limit' entries, preserving order. Never invent runbook ids outside RB-01..RB-30 range.
